newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Harvest weighs on prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Harvest weighs on prices.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mostly steady to lower, pressured by bountiful supplies of newly-harvested soft red winter and hard red winter wheat for milling, millfeed dealers said.
Carolina sources said soft red winter wheat was locally priced 10 to 15 cents per bushel less than corn, plus high quality of this year's wheat made it an attractive feed ingredient.
USDA on Friday estimated the U.S. winter wheat crop at 1.78 billion bushels, up 20 percent from a year ago.
Grain dealers said both the hard red winter and soft red winter wheat harvests were producing grain with high test weights, low moisture and very little disease.
Much of the harvested wheat was going to flour mills rather than to export. Also, many mills were running through the weekend in some areas, dealers said.
